metadata.title: Reduced C*-algebras of the Thompson family: an attributed consequence of nonamenability
metadata.native_Description: An attributed consequence note applying OpenAI's nonamenability theorem for standard Thompson F to the published equivalences of Le Boudec and Matte Bon. The reduced group C*-algebras of F, T, the full automorphism group Aut(F), and the abstract commensurator Comm(F) are simple and have their canonical traces as their unique tracial states, by the discrete-group trace theorem of Breuillard, Kalantar, Kennedy and Ozawa. The countable standard circle-overgroup consequence is also recorded. All these simplicity reductions are inherited; T's unique trace was already unconditional. No new simplicity criterion, independent proof of nonamenability, or first-priority claim is made. The conclusions depending on the new input have exactly the same dependency on its validity. The source proof was manually audited; actual Lean source and semantics were inspected, but no fresh Lean kernel build was reproduced owing to insufficient disk space, and the follow-on theorem is not claimed to be formalized. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. This preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing; automated adversarial audits are not human peer review.

an attributed consequence of nonamenability
Alec Kriebel
October 6, 2026
Abstract
Combining OpenAI’s announced nonamenability theorem for the standard Thompson group
F with the published equivalences of Le Boudec and Matte Bon gives simplicity of the reduced
group C*-algebras of F , T , Aut(F ) and the abstract commensurator Comm(F ). Their canonical
traces are their unique tracial states by the discrete-group trace theorem of Breuillard, Kalantar,
Kennedy and Ozawa. We record the exact hypotheses, countability and attribution, and the
corresponding consequence for countable circle-homeomorphism overgroups of the standard ac-
tion. The argument is an application of established reductions, not a new simplicity criterion or
an independent proof of nonamenability. Unique trace for T was already known unconditionally.
All conclusions involving the new input have exactly the same dependency on its validity.
1    Scope, deﬁnitions and inherited inputs
All groups carry the discrete topology. Thompson’s group F consists of the increasing piecewise-
linear homeomorphisms of [0, 1] with ﬁnitely many pieces, dyadic breakpoints and slopes in 2Z .
It ﬁxes both endpoints. Identifying them realizes the standard subgroup F ≤ Homeo(S1 ), where
S1 = R/Z. Thompson’s group T consists of orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms with
ﬁnitely many dyadic linear pieces, slopes in 2Z and preservation of the dyadic points. Thus the
speciﬁed F is a subgroup of T .
Here Aut(F ) is the full abstract automorphism group, including orientation-reversing automor-
phisms in its line realization. The abstract commensurator Comm(F ) is formed from isomorphisms
between ﬁnite-index subgroups of F , with two identiﬁed if their restrictions agree on some common
ﬁnite-index subgroup. Composition after restriction gives its group law. These are the full groups
in [2, Corollary 4.4], not just their orientation-preserving subgroups. Faithful line realizations are
described by Brin and by Burillo–Cleary–Röver [5, 6].

metadata.title: The Sperner property of standard graded Artinian complete intersections in characteristic zero
metadata.native_Description: For every standard graded Artinian complete intersection over an arbitrary characteristic-zero field, the maximum minimal number of generators over all ideals, including nonhomogeneous ideals, equals the largest coefficient of the complete-intersection Hilbert series. This concise note records an immediate consequence of OpenAI's Artinian EGH theorem and the previously published EGH-to-Sperner implication of Harima, Wachi and Watanabe. It makes degree-one elimination, the empty/all-linear case, the all-ideal filtration argument and field scope explicit, with exact integer examples and scoped dependency/priority audits. No new EGH proof, first-priority claim, Lefschetz theorem, nongraded extension or unrestricted positive-characteristic conclusion is asserted. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. Automated adversarial reviews are not conventional human peer review; this preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing at publication. No formalization of the follow-on theorem is claimed.

Artinian complete intersections in characteristic zero
Alec Kriebel
October 6, 2026
Abstract
We record the Sperner property for every standard graded Artinian complete intersection
over an arbitrary characteristic-zero ﬁeld: the maximum minimal number of generators of an
ideal, including nonhomogeneous ideals, equals the largest coeﬃcient of its complete-intersection
Hilbert series. The result is an immediate consequence of OpenAI’s Artinian Eisenbud–Green–
Harris theorem and the previously published implication of Harima, Wachi, and Watanabe. We
give an explicit account of that implication, eliminate degree-one generators, justify the passage
to all ideals by the associated graded ﬁltration, and verify the ﬁeld scope. No new proof of EGH
or new Lefschetz assertion is claimed.

maxj dimk Aj . The ideals in this deﬁnition include 0, A, and nonhomogeneous ideals.

metadata.title: No single polynomial inequality defines a real binary Gram locus
metadata.native_Description:
For a real tensor with n binary factors, the Gram locus is the tuple of determinants of its one-mode Gram matrices as the tensor ranges over the closed Frobenius unit ball. For every n>=3, no single real polynomial nonnegativity condition in those determinant coordinates defines this locus inside the cube [0,1/4]^n, or inside its known convex hull. This gives a negative answer to Seigal's single-polynomial question for n>=4. The self-contained proof uses established marginal polygon inequalities, an explicit real three-factor realization, exact polynomial multiplicities and zero-determinant slices. A strictly positive rational four-factor tuple also passes the proposed polynomial condition but is unrealizable at any allowed norm.

The marginal criteria and real constructions of Higuchi-Sudbery-Szulc, Bravyi and Domanov-Stegeman-De Lathauwer are credited antecedents. Sinn's earlier general boundary/interior obstruction is also credited. Alper Ferudun's unrefereed October 2, 2026 preprint, DOI10.5281/zenodo.23111048, contains an overlapping stronger theorem, including an all-positive domain. Our original theorem-bearing proof is present in GitHub PR170, created September 30, 2026 at13:15:23UTC, and is unchanged. We describe these as contemporaneous separate disclosures. Commit timestamps are author-controlled; current public repository visibility was verified, but historical visibility was not independently archived. This October12 formal preprint is not backdated. Mutual independence of authorship, literal simultaneity, exclusive firstness and complete historical novelty are not certified. The accompanying bounded priority audit records exact source versions, read coverage and access limits.

The deposit contains the manuscript PDF and a support archive with standalone LaTeX, exact standard-library controls, ordinary and optimized outputs, deliberately false variants, chronology evidence and priority reviews. Finite controls supplement the universal written proof; they cannot prove an all-polynomial impossibility or certify historical priority. AI tools were used extensively in solving, drafting, source comparison, reproduction and adversarial verification. This work is unrefereed and has not undergone conventional human peer review. The author is responsible for its contents.
